text:
dora-research: Heads up — I found weights for a community model called 'bramble-8b' (github.com/forestai/bramble). The attached LICENSE.txt says: `research-only, no commercial hosting, no redistribution of weights`.
ben-legal: Short answer: that language blocks us from offering bramble-8b on our paid Hosted API. 'No commercial use' covers paid inference.
ben-legal: Also important — "no redistribution of weights" usually means we cannot store or transfer the checkpoint to customer buckets or public repos.
alice-ml: For clarification — what about running internal evals or quantization experiments under our dev credits? Can we run them and keep the artifacts behind our internal storage? :thinking_face:
ben-legal: Internal evaluation for research purposes is often allowed, but we should keep it strictly internal and timebox it. Quantized checkpoints are borderline — creating a quantized binary could be treated as a derivative or redistribution depending on the exact wording. If the license forbids redistribution but allows local modification for research, it might be fine to quantize for internal experiments, but we should NOT push quantized weights to any S3 bucket accessible outside the research team or to customer environments.
chris-ops: Operational question — we sometimes convert weights during a Private deployment (customer brings model, we optimize/quantize for performance). If the customer provides the weights, does generating a quantized copy on their Private instance count as redistribution by us?
ben-legal: If the customer supplies the original checkpoint directly into their VPC (they upload), and we perform in-place optimization inside that VPC without copying to our control plane, that is typically allowed. The red line is when we take custody and transfer or store modified copies on our infrastructure. For Dedicated/Hosted where we manage the files, that likely violates the 'no redistribution' clause.
dora-research: So recommended operational path: do not add bramble-8b to the public model catalog, mark it as "license: research-only" in our internal registry, and require a legal OK before any hosting. We still want to run small evals (perplexity, instruction-following) to decide whether to request permission upstream.
ben-legal: Agreed. I'll draft an upstream permission request. Suggested ask: (1) permission to host bramble-8b on commercial SaaS, (2) permission to redistribute performance-optimized (quantized) variants to customers under contract, (3) attribution requirements.
alice-ml: Can you drop a short email template I can send to maintainers? I'll include eval logs and a short business case.
ben-legal: Sure — use this template and attach the eval report.

````
Subject: Permission request: commercial hosting & optimized weights for 'bramble-8b'

Hi maintainers,

We're engineers at Redwood Inference (https://redwood.ai). We've been evaluating bramble-8b for serving real-time inference. Your LICENSE currently states "research-only, no commercial hosting, no redistribution of weights."

Could you confirm whether you'd be willing to grant Redwood the following rights under a simple mutual agreement?
1) Allow Redwood to host bramble-8b behind our commercial API (paid customers).
2) Permit us to create and distribute performance-optimized/quantized variants to customers under a contract that preserves attribution and does not allow further redistribution.
3) Any required attribution text or other constraints we should include in our docs.

We can offer back a short compliance report and attribution block. Happy to sign a CLA or a small addendum.

Thanks,
Ben Legal on behalf of Redwood Inference
````

chris-ops: Nice. From infra side: until we get permission, we'll block model ingestion pipelines from persisting the checkpoint to shared S3 buckets and tag any experiment as `bramble-licensed:research-only`.
dora-research: I'll run a short eval job in an isolated sandbox with ephemerally mounted weights and post results here. If maintainers come back, we can escalate to commercial terms.

ops-bot: :warning: Model registered: bramble-8b flagged as `needs-legal-review` in internal model-registry (ID: mdl-202509-bramble).
alice-ml: One more thing — for our product teams asking about Dedicated vs Private: we should document that Private (customer-provided weights, no transfer to Redwood) is the safer route, but sales must get legal approval for any assistance we provide in weight modification or packaging.
ben-legal: I'll add a short note to the legal playbook and create a checklist: upstream-permission-request, eval-sandbox logs, no-persist S3 guardrails, and contract clause for customer-supplied weights.

dora-research: Thanks all. I'll post the eval summary once it's done. :eyes:
